newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran calls for international action on Afghanistan.
newsitem.headline: Iran calls for international action on Afghanistan.

text.p: Iranian state radio on Thursday called for urgent international action to avoid a humanitarian tragedy in neighbouring Afghanistan where a battle is raging over the capital Kabul.

"World bodies including the United Nations Security Council have expressed concern over the situation in Afghanistan...But the Afghan situation is beyond expressions of concern and requires urgent and serious action," Tehran radio said.

"If the situation continues in this way a humanitarian tragedy is not beyond expectation (due to) the uncertain future and the approach of the cold season and the lack of food, fuel and medicine," the radio said in a commentary.
U.N. Security Council members called on Wednesday for an end to the fighting in Afghanistan and for peace talks between the government and the Taleban militia fighting to capture Kabul.

The radio did not say what kind of action was needed, but reiterated Tehran's stand that there could be no military solution to the conflict and that the Kabul government and opposition groups should seek a negotiated settlement.
Iran has supported the Kabul government as legitimate. It has been hostile to the Taleban, whom Iranian media have accused of being manipulated by Pakistan and the United States.
But Iran's media appear to have toned down their criticism of the Taleban in the past few weeks and Iranian officials have held talks with representatives of the Islamic militia.
